text_fidelity_a:
Bezier Games Palace of Mad King Ludwig Palaces of Mad King Ludwig is a tile-laying, castle-building game for two to four players. This game is reminiscent of Carcassonne, except it is a good bit more complicated, requiring players to place building tiles near each other in specific patterns to earn swans of various colors, utilize special powers or scoring rules, and to build both above and below ground while the moat around the castle continually encloses your playspace.

Ultimately, while the components are nice quality, there are quite a lot of bits for a game like this, and the artwork is not particularly interesting. Rooms are largely void of identifiable decoration, making the words easy to read, but the rooms difficult to distinguish. Also of note, in the previous "Mad King" game, a major selling point of the game was mismatched and oddly sized tiles, while this one is entirely composed of squares and rectangles.

All told, we fell like this was a solid game, but one that has just a few too many rules that confine what you can do and what you want to do. Most of the time, there was a clear "best move" available, and rarely were more than, say, three decisions even possible based on what you could buy and where you could place it. I think a lot of people will like this game more than I did, as my fellow players certainly did. I would personally rather play something that is more streamlined (Carcassonne), or simply more interesting (Castles of Mad King Ludwig).

Also of note, Palace of Mad King Ludwig is not related to it's cousin "Castles," which is a little confusing. The idea behind the games is radically different.
text_fidelity_b: Bezier Games Palace of Mad King Ludwig

text_fidelity_a:
Scrabble Deluxe (EA) The special part of this particular version of Scrabble is the fact that the case is also the game. It's easy to keep everything together with this case, and it has grip-like places at the top that make toting the case around easy.

The case is hard plastic and it simply unfolds to reveal the game board, which is also plastic. The board is designed so that the tiles are placed within a square spot, and won't move around or get jarred out of place easily. Wheels are attached to the bottom(or each side of the case) to make turning the board in a circle easier. If the player wants to pull the board towards them, these wheels won't make that task easier. The wheels are turned a bit, making the board turn in a circle, not a line.

On each side of the case are drawers that pull out. These drawers are actually pretty roomy. These hold the tiles and the tile holders. The tile holders are plastic, and come within a velvet-like drawstring bag. The tiles are wooden.

Overall, this isn't the prettiest or fanciest of games. Despite being called "Deluxe", don't expect a glamorous version. It IS designed to make playing scrabble a little easier, though.
text_fidelity_b: Scrabble Deluxe (EA)

text_fidelity_a:
PLANET BAKE Vegan Donut Making Kit - Plant-Based, Gluten Free Donut Kit with Pre-Measured Ingredients & Silicone Donut Molds - Complete Kids Baking Set for Ages 4-12 (Vanilla) I also tried the chocolate version of this donut kit and was quite disappointed in the taste of the donuts. This vanilla option is much better. In anticipation of less than ideal taste I added some good quality vanilla extract which also helped boost the flavor.

Still, the issues I had with the chocolate version are also present in this version. The box it comes in is cheap and flimsy, and dented up quite a bit in transit. It makes for a poor presentation should this be a gift item. On the plus side, the sprinkle packet stayed closed in the vanilla kit box (it broke open in the chocolate kit box and there were sprinkles everywhere). The frosting packet is inside the main pouch with loose flour, so it's a messy proposition to get the frosting packet out -- flour spills easily. Lastly, the silicone molds are quite flimsy. Putting them into something supportive, such as a muffin tin, is highly recommended prior to filling and baking.

The vanilla donuts have a much better flavor than the chocolate, especially when additional vanilla extract is added. The assembly process is simple and, while kids will need supervision (especially when dealing with the silicone molds) it's a fun activity.

Taking all the pros and cons into consideration puts my score at 3.5 stars. It's a great idea, but some of the kinks need to be ironed out to make it a kit that is worth the price charged.
text_fidelity_b: PLANET BAKE Vegan Donut Making Kit - Plant-Based, Gluten Free Donut Kit with Pre-Measured Ingredients & Silicone Donut Molds - Complete Kids Baking Set for Ages 4-12 (Vanilla)

Monopoly Board Game The Classic Edition, 2-8 players I have many fond memories of playing "Monopoly" with siblings, cousins, and parents when I was child and then with my own family as an adult. This version is very close to the version I remember playing in the 70s. The game board and tokens are sturdy, and my favorite tokens from when I played as a kid are included - the dog, the horse, and the race car, along with the shoe, hat, thimble, iron, wheelbarrow. Two others are included that I don't remember at all - a cannon and a ship.

The game comes with rules for the standard, full length game. Players choose a token and go around the board purchasing property and building houses and hotels, hoping to force their opponents into bankruptcy. This game can be played by two or more players.

The property title deeds are still made of thin cardboard, but may be a little more flimsy than older versions. The money tray is even better than it used to be. It's made of plastic and seems like it will hold up much better than the old flat tray with the flimsy dividers that used to quickly fall apart. The only thing that is off for me is the color of the Community Chest cards. They are a yellow-orange color instead of the yellow I am used to. I don't know if the very first version of the game had cards this color or not, but this is the first time I've seen this.

If you're looking to replace your old game or haven't played the original version, you can't go wrong with this classic game.
text_fidelity_b: Monopoly Board Game The Classic Edition, 2-8 players

The Return too home when low on Battery functioned well as I flew the bird too that point almost everytime, there was an issue with the follow me I should have had it up a little higher it did hit a branch on a tree which was my fault because these drones do not come with obstacle avoidance and it took a fall to the ground no worse for wear I stopped the motors flipped back over unlock the motors and she went right back up no issues. Photo quality really really love the camera and take some great pictures even out that 400 ft. I really like the 4K camera and the quality of the video and pictures ( all photos post are unedited) and this unit also allows you to record record audio which is pretty good for bloggers , though my one gripe is I wish the 270 came with a gimbal to really make exceptional video, but at this price point it's a trade off!

The HS270 is very very wind resistant I flew this in pretty high winds somewhere between 15 to maybe 18 miles an hour and some strong gusts I thought for sure it going to blow over the pond or even into some of the trees. The GPS worked awesome as it kept the unit in its place and even though in my video it was shaky because you could see the wind is blowing it all over the place I was thoroughly impressed and this bird should not fly away from you unless you accidentally turn off the GPS in which case you really need to know how to fly this thing or any drones in the wind with the GPS off. It has a 3-speed future from low medium to high I enjoyed that it seemed like when it was windy I kicked it in high speed and it flew alot better keeping in medium most of the other times I enjoy a quick flights back and forth but was able to enjoy the roughly 21 minutes of flying time at the most and less on that really windy day it was only about 16 minutes most of the time it was fighting the wind. It takes pretty good pictures fpv to the cell phone like 720pvideo and 2K photo But the quality really comes to life when you have a SD card in the unit.

I think overall this unit does exactly as it's advertised to do and being able to fold up you can actually take this thing with you on vacation put in your suitcase carry out with you when you go on a hike and have something with you besides your camera that you can put up into the air and taking it up sectional a different view all of your vacation or a picture of you and your family or significant other standing by a Mountain or even the Grand Canyon with a drone from a distance and capture something that cant be done with a selfie stick. So I recommend this unit, but make sure you get extra batteries cuz it does take a while with the USB plug to charge the battery, most times it took 2-3 hours till fully charged. I grabbed a case on Amazon which I believe it was a case setup for a DJI mavic I did a little modifying on the sides of the hard foam and it was able to sit down in the case well which I showed the picture in the reviews it was the soyan case for like 22 bucks or something like that. All in all a great deal, I'm totally satisfied!

text_fidelity_a:
Radio Flyer Kid & Cargo with Canopy, Folding Wagon with 2 Versatile Seats, (Amazon Exclusive) (3965Z), Red The Canopy and two seats (that can easily be used or not as your needs change) with seatbelts features take this from a standard utility cart to a multi-purpose cart that is good for both transporting stuff and transporting kids. Even when out in the sun. Also the end storage net is very nice because even if the kids take up a big chunk of the available space, you can still store a bag or two or three depending on how well you pack. On the other end the two drink holders mean you don’t have to carry your drinks. Handy if you have kids prone to tossing bottles around as they’ll be within easy reach of you, but not in eyesight of the little ones.

Although it is more useful in that sense than some other carts, it does have some faults. The Velcro that holds the handle against the cart when not in use is almost more trouble than it’s worth. It’s not very sturdy, so if you even lightly bump the handle, it pops the Velcro open and the handle falls. Also the seams at the bottoms are exposed instead of being finished properly, leaving it more open to fraying or damage. The wheels are much larger than most utility carts, so the turning radius isn’t as good as our other carts. Going down a hill, it almost wants to get away from you, though that is an issue with most carts. The canopy is useful but works almost like slap bracelets, so getting it to stay is tricky at first, I’d almost prefer straps that just hold it in place around the retractable poles.

Overall, this is not a perfect cart, but it still very nice despite its faults. The canopy is optional and takes up almost no storage space because the poles are retractable into the cart, so you only need to roll up the fabric and stick in the net storage. The seats are perfect for young kids. It can go back and forth between kiddie wagon and an ideal cart for things like flea markets.

I was torn on the star rating, and rounded up to 4. I’d actually put this at about a 3.5. Do keep in mind that it doesn’t come with any tools, so you’ll need your own (a hammer, a wrench, and a screwdriver).
text_fidelity_b: Radio Flyer Kid & Cargo with Canopy, Folding Wagon with 2 Versatile Seats, (Amazon Exclusive) (3965Z), Red

text_fidelity_a:
Name 5 Game This is, hands down, the worst game I have ever played for several reasons that all share a central theme of poorly laid out rules. I will share the 2 most glaring flaws from my experience w/ this gem of a game.

#1 A large portion of the categories are so subjective as to make them unplayable. For example, one of the categories in the game is, "Vacation Destinations." Who is to say that literally anything I say is not a valid answer? I could just name any destination on the planet. Who is to say I DON'T want to vacation in Darfur or at my ex-girlfriend's house? This is just one example, there are literally hundreds of categories where anything you say could be construed as a valid answer. The rules are ambiguous and fall back on self-policing as a substitute for a well thought out set of guidelines. The lack of a set of coherent rules leads to an endless debate about the validity of the players' answers that becomes incredibly boring to watch and incredibly frustrating to participate in.

#2 The arguments over what is and what is not a valid answer aside, an average round of this game takes about 10 minutes to play through. So unless you feel like going through the aggravation of playing more than once, you're not getting much bang for your buck. HOWEVER, it is worth noting that portions of this game can run on ad infinitum; one of the poorly engineered "challenges" in this game is to square off against another team to name as many items w/in the category chosen, obviously the one who runs out of ideas loses the challenge. Sounds like a decent idea, BUT instead of placing a time limit and perhaps writing down as many ideas as you can think of, like w/ Scattergories, this game has you go back-and-forth in a turn-taking verbal manner. The category we squared off w/ was "Foods That Begin With A." My god, the list went on and on for 10 minutes before everyone got bored and just called that round a tie. These challenges will not appear in every game; if you have the bad luck of stumbling into this challenge during your game, I advise you to get out a book or go make a sandwich while the teams face-off.

My advice to those considering this game is to buy Taboo or Scattergories instead. These two games are in the same genre and are time-tested winners w/ a clear set of rules. This game needs to be re-engineered with some attention paid to making the categories more thought-provoking and objective. I would recommend this game for parents with 5 year olds that just want to let their kids mess around and yell out random things for 10 minutes.
text_fidelity_b: Name 5 Game

Educational Insights Hot Dots Let's Learn Kindergarten Math: Amazon Exclusive Kindergarten Math Workbook, Ages 5+ & Hot Dots Let's Master Grade 1 Reading with Talking Pen Very educational with great building-blocks for math success. The actual concepts focused in this activity book are great, but there are two areas of improvement outside of the lessons:

The Pen—My child tends to hold it in the middle or more toward the top, and the sound button always seems to get turned off. I don’t really know of a better placement for this button, but it’s worth mentioning. Maybe one of those slider buttons would be better at preventing the sound being turned off so easily.

The dots themselves don't seem very small, but still seem to cause us some issues when in use. Since the pen is quite large, my kiddo will often choose the right answer, put the pen down on the dot, but miss the dot slightly which then gives us a red light and a “sad” beep. Even though the answer is right, missing the dot makes you think that you’re wrong because you get the red light and sad sound. I then have to say “try that dot again” and reassure that the answer is correct. I do wish the dots were just a little bit larger to give the pen a broader area to make contact with the dot. It's not a major issue, as most of the time we do hit the dot just fine, but it's also something I've noticed that has happened several times.

Otherwise, these books are awesome, very educational and a lot of fun! More of 4.5 Stars for us.

text_fidelity_a:
World Series of Yahtzee Board Games [[VIDEOID:9706f008dc0f922f2a22889963de0e00]] This is a digital, board-based game of Yahtzee. I think it's made to compete with [[ASIN:B0042ET8S0 Uno Attack Game]] and [[ASIN:B001G5431A Bunco]], and it is much more fun than both of those games. Sometimes making a classic into a digital version is a mistake, but the designers did an awesome job with this game.

It's still [[ASIN:B00000IWH6 Yahtzee]]. You still get five dice, and you have to match the classic Yahtzee combinations of Yahtzee (five of a kind), four of a kind, three of a kind, full house, small straight (sequence or run) and large straight. But, everybody plays at once with their own sets of five dice, and the computer in the middle moderates everything, so goes very quickly and it's exciting.

The little buzzer in the middle is pretty sophisticated for a simple computer. It records who buzzes in and in which order you buzzed in, and it plays some fun countdown music. You get five seconds after the first person finishes to finish rolling and to buzz in yourself. Each person can collect up to one card per turn, based on what they rolled, but if you're not lucky, or if someone else gets your combination first, then you don't get any cards per turn. Usually turns take about thirty seconds each, and a full game all the way through will take about ten minutes, so it's very fast paced and fun.

I really liked the original Yahtzee, and I really like this too.

Pros:
+Very fun new version of an already fun classic
+Doesn't waste paper like the old version
+No more waiting around for slow players, like the old version
+You really should start playing this instead of Bunco, since there's a lot more strategy in this game
+You can roll the dice as many times as you want, where in traditional Yahtzee, you could only roll the dice three times per turn

Cons:
-The black dice with the red dots are so much cooler than the rest of the dice, so everyone will be fighting over these
-Made out of cheap plastic cardboard. If you love this game, which you probably will, and if you're not a dainty family, which you probably aren't, then you'll break these pretty quickly and go through about one of these games per year. It's still cheaper than a night at the movies, though, and this game is fun enough to justify getting a new one.
text_fidelity_b: World Series of Yahtzee Board Games

Patchwork | Strategy / Puzzle Game | Family Board Game | Two Player Game for Kids and Adults | Ages 8 and up |Average Playtime 30 Minutes | Made by Lookout Games , Brown Easy to learn, fast to play, and fraught with surprisingly difficult decisions. The basic premise of putting together a quilt becomes very complex when you're weighing interesting opportunity costs on every single action. At the end of the game, everything boils down to how many buttons you've collected versus how much space on your quilt is unpatched by the time you reach the end of game board with a finite number of spaces. Do I spend a small amount of buttons to fill a large section of my quilt? Do I spend more buttons to fill less quilt with a patch that gives me more income but may move me more towards ending the game too prematurely for victory? Do I not buy any patches, and just advance along the board and collect buttons? It's shockingly complex and interesting considering the simplicity of the mechanics.

I'm a big fan of two player games, as it's great for my wife and I to always have something to do together. This is particularly great for the two of us because set-up is fast and the rules are simple enough that you never waste time referencing the instructions. So we even get to play on busy weeknights.

Journey Girls 18" Doll, Meredith The Journey Girls dolls are 18" dolls. Clothing-wise, they appear to be compatible with other 18" dolls such as American Girl, Playtime by Eimmie, the Our Generation dolls, or even the 18" Adora dolls. At this price point, they are definitely an affordable play option for younger girls. Like the Adora dolls, they have plastic shoulder and upper torso area and the lower torso is cloth. (The AG, Playtime by Eimmie, and Our Generation dolls all have completely cloth torsos). The Journey Girls dolls do not turn their head well, but their face sculpts are all unique to each doll (again, similar to the Adora dolls, as the Playtime by Eimmie seem to all have the same face sculpt with different skin shades and paint jobs). I personally find the Adora dolls to be my favorite 18" alternative to the American Girl dolls, but they are still at a high enough price point that I would not want to hand one over to my 5 year old for unsupervised play. The Playtime by Eimmie dolls have a full cloth body, making them softer and more huggable than the Journey Girls dolls (and probably more appealing for younger girls), and they are about the same price point. The style of clothing the Journey Girls have, as well as their sculpted plastic upper torsos, they give the impression of teenagers rather than younger girls, which makes them very appealing to the 8-10 year old set.

Meredith is absolutely beautiful and my daughters love her glamorous clothing and hairstyle. An affordable 18" doll option that doesn't make me cringe to give to impulsive young girls for play.
text_fidelity_b: Journey Girls 18" Doll, Meredith

text_fidelity_a:
Thames & Kosmos Crystal Growing Science Kit Grow Over A Dozen Crystals with 15 Experiments, Includes Storage Case & 32 Page Color Laboratory Manual My child's science project last year was growing crystals. We had lots of fun using different temperature liquids, chemicals, etc. to see which would grow fastest, best, make the most solid of crystals and even made rock candy as a "take home" treat. I love the creativity of this kit. It allows for you to create UP TO 13 different experiments (but if you cheat you can get a couple more out of it). Some of the chemicals used are not safe for young kids so I'd highly suggest sticking to the recommended manufacturer's age. Not to mention the fact that some of the crystals will take longer than a week to fully form -- most kids don't have the patience to wait. Not waiting the proper amount of time to ensure the solidity of the crystals will result in disappointment as you can imagine something that isn't solid enough can break very easy. Following directions is paramount! Make sure you sit with your child and read through all of the instructions before beginning. I'd suggest sticking with the easiest project first to get their feet wet on experimenting then gradually go through the "harder" ones. I do like that the simple purchase of extra chemicals (or using sugar) can add a lot more fun to your kit. Thames & Kosmos is a good company. They even provide online printable instructions along side the greatly illustrated manual. http://www.thamesandkosmos.com/news/manualsamples/659127_glowingcrystals_manual_sample.pdf
The price of the kit is very fair. In fact, I'd say it would be an excellent science fair project to conduct with your child this spring. Start practicing now and wow the judges with modified versions. Just be sure to do your homework. Check out books from your local library on growing crystals and start taking notes. This could be a really fun learning experience for grade-schoolers and homeschoolers alike. The only thing I thought was slightly cheesy was the "treasure case" and the shapes (thus my four stars). But kids will get a kick out of them.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos Crystal Growing Science Kit Grow Over A Dozen Crystals with 15 Experiments, Includes Storage Case & 32 Page Color Laboratory Manual

Mainstreet Classics Dutchman 3-in-1 Combo Folding Board Game Set The board is a very nice, stained wood. It measures 15.75" by 15.75" (including the handles) wide by 1" deep when open or 2" when folded. It folds in half, with the recessed backgammon side holding the game pieces during storage. Two pairs of magnets hold the board closed when folded. The magnets have been effective at holding the set closed without being difficult to open when desired. The top board is 8 by 8 squares across. The wood checkers are just under 1" across and have a slight protrusion on the bottom to keep them in place when a piece is crowned. There are 15 pieces each of brown and white, and these pieces are also used for backgammon. The wood chess pieces are common, simple chess shapes and have a felt bottom. The pawns are 1 3/8" tall and the king is 3" tall. The set also includes two wooden cups, two pairs of dice, and a doubling cube for backgammon. The included game instructions are brief and not really enough to learn to play the games, but it's easy enough to find this information online. From the box: "Solid wood travel set accented with walnut, maple, and mahogany playing surfaces" as well as the California Prop 65 warning with "Wash hands after use."

There are some 1 star reviews for this set, and I have a hard time believing it's for the same set. The set I got has lovely workmanship and everything looks sturdy and well-made. The handle is plenty wide (4.25" across and 1" high) and is sanded smooth as well as finished with a stain. There is no obvious glue.

This is the ideal sized container. The larger containers have too much doh for small hands.

This is a great set of colors. Some of the colors (like black, brown, and white) are hard to find in smaller sets.

Fisher-Price Disney's Jake and The Never Land Pirates - Jake's Musical Pirate Ship Bucky [Amazon Exclusive] My oldest son turns 4 in just over a week, and he absolutely LOVES this toy! It's one of the few toys that he goes back for again and again.

There are two doors on the ship. One is to the back of the cabin and one is over "tick-tock"(the crocodile) who pops out with the press of a button. These doors come off pretty easily, BUT they pop right back on just as easily. There's also 3 "missiles" that shoot out of the cannon on the front of the boat with the press of a button. These worked great for us, but to be honest, those small pieces get lost pretty quickly. My son usually plays with the ship without those.

My favorite feature is the pegs that are placed ALL over the ship. There are little holes on the bottom of Jake and Skully's feet, so you can place them on the pegs and hold them in place while playing. There's even a little clear bar at the very top of the ship that you can put them on, so it looks like they're flying. I think it's a really cool feature!! I also really like the "rocking" motion of the ship when it moves. It kind of wobbles back and forth to look like it's floating on waves.

My only complaints is the sound, first of all. The music sounds kind of like it's coming from cheap speakers, and I find it annoying. My son loves it and likes to press the buttons to hear the music and phrases. If you really didn't like that feature, the batteries could be taken out. There are stickers on the side of the boat of Izzy and Cubby to look like they are looking out the window waving. I guess that's an attempt to make up for not having them as figurines. I know that you can buy separate figurines, but I don't know if they have pegs on the bottom of their feet to work with this ship.

Overall, our whole family gives it 2 thumbs up! We all love it, and definitely recommend it.

text_fidelity_a:
Marvel Guardians of The Galaxy Big Blastin' Rocket Raccoon Figure, 10 Inch I'm going to review this not from the perspective of a toy, but rather as a piece of movie memorabilia. Years ago, I use to love to go to the local mall here in Austin and stop by the SunCoast Motion Picture Company store. Where you could buy all sort of movie related items as well as the movies themselves. Over the years I've bought a number of items very similar to this Rocket Raccoon figure for my collection. So when I was offered one of these 10 inch figure to check out I gladly accepted.

I wasn't expecting this figure to be so big - I knew it was suppose to be 10" but it seems bigger than that to me. It came in one of those open face boxes that allow you to actually touch the toy before taking it out of the box, and you can activate the sound effect as the item ships with the batteries already installed and the sound box is set in a demo mode. The sounds it make are pretty loud, they should put a smile on any child face (and a frown on any adults in the room).

Once out of the box, there is some assembly required. You have to pop the tail into the figures rear-end (yeah, I know). It takes some effort to do that, so I suggest having an adult do it. Other than that, the figure is ready to go. Like I mentioned there is a demo mode on the effects box. The effects are controlled with a three-position switch - Off, Try Me (demo), and On. The unit is powered by three double-A batteries which are located in the figures backpack (there is a screw securing the cover to the batteries). Once you turn on the power switch, there are two activation points - one on the figures leg and another on top of the gun he is holding. Pressing one or the other activates both motion and sound effects, plus the figure speaks phrases from the movie. The motion effects are just the end of the gun rotating and the figure shaking a bit. There are some light effects with the end of the gun & gun sight lighting up. There aren't that many spoken phrases - so they can get a bit repetitive after awhile.

The toy is pretty well made - a lot more substantial than most of the movie memorabilia, but then again it was made for kids to play with.

I kept the figure on my desk at work for about a week before bringing it home. I can't tell you how times people stopped and played with the figure (too many times, as that is what prompted me to finally take it home). I haven't seen the movie yet - but it is definitely one that I plan on seeing this summer.

I really like this figure - about the only thing I could comment on would be the detail of the end of his gun, everything else has a decent level of detail, but that part of the gun doesn't. Guessing that is more due to the fact that they made it out of clear plastic so that the light effect could be seen.
text_fidelity_b: Marvel Guardians of The Galaxy Big Blastin' Rocket Raccoon Figure, 10 Inch

text_fidelity_a:
Monopoly Empire Game [[VIDEOID:8f653ee987e2df8b52e209e097da8a22]] This is such a cool game! It's a scaled down version of Monopoly, and each game only takes 5-15 minutes to play, instead of the hours of a regular Monopoly game. So you'll hear something with this Monopoly game that you won't hear with any other Monopoly game, which is "Want to play again?"

It still captures the essence of Monopoly, so it still feels like a Monopoly game. It's more of a social game than a strategy game, but that will make it more fun for more people.

They've taken out the property cards, and replaced them with little tiles and a tower. The number of tiles, not the original value of the tile, determine how much that you pay when you land on someone else's property. The old Community Chest cards are now Empire cards, and you get a couple to hold on to at the start of the game, and you can use these strategically, and do various combos with them.

It's very fun, and I liked it a lot. If you get just one game this year, this should be the game you pick.

Pros:
+Excellent instructions
+Extremely well designed
+Has cool brands like Fender, Nerf, and Coke
+Quick version of Monopoly (I never thought I'd ever use quick and Monopoly in the same sentence.)
+They did an awesome job of play testing this game. It's very balanced and very fun. Whoever worked on the team that made this game should be promoted.

Cons:
-Less strategy than regular Monopoly, but it is more fun for more people
-Because it's subsidized by advertising, they really should be giving this game away. But, the advertising isn't as annoying as in other games.
text_fidelity_b: Monopoly Empire Game

text_fidelity_a:
Enso Rings Disney Lilo & Stitch Silicone Ring Collection - Comfortable and Flexible Design - Ohana and Experiment 626 I wear a silicone ring and truly like it. Perhaps prefer it because I don't worry about it like I do gold or silver, nor do I tend to hook it (sometimes painfully) on things. I recently noticed the Enso Rings Collections and liked much of what I saw, so when I spotted this Enso Rings Disney Lilo and Stitch Silicone Ring Collection available I grabbed it. In this case, for my wife. I am a Disney fan as well, but Stitch is one of her favorites, and honestly, I was not a big fan of the red - I prefer blue or black in silicone and the traditional silvers and golds. So... how would we like this Enso Rings Disney Lilo and Stitch Silicone Ring Collection?

1. It arrived in a nice little packaging making great for protecting the ring, displaying the ring, and a nice presentation for gifting. Great all around.

2. Sizing. Honestly, this was the hardest part. Sizing your finger is never the easiest of tasks as we have discovered. But in this case they wanted the inside of a ring rather than your finger. We have a flexible, cloth type measuring tape, but still, trying to get that in there and with the metal end and lined up and staying in place as you pull it out.. not fun. They do have their sizes to the rounded whole - I feel like I remember others with in between sizes, which would make this harder. In the end we went with the one we got consistently and hoped. Turned out great - fits my wife's middle finger as she wanted and my ring finger.

3. The red is actually pretty cool. Again, not my favorite on the spectrum of ring colors, but my wife loves it and I like it. And for the Lilo and Stitch option, it works. There is a sparkle to it - both nice and not overwhelming.

4. The in-print on the ring feels "subtle," but present; something you can see, but at a glance it's more like a light-shadow affect. Upon closer examination you spot the little Lilo (not a fave character for either of us), but the Stitch rocks. And the little flower brings out the Polynesian flavor, while giving the whole thing a sweet nod to Disney. For a Disney fan, it's a great find.

5. This is my wife's first silicone, but like me, she's liking it. It is comfortable, easy to wear, does not catch on things in the same way (but all rings do catch), and it has that silicone flexibility that makes wearing it more comfortable in many situations.

6. I have found in wearing silicone I have to be more careful when washing my hands. Soap can build up behind and/or keep up the wetness between ring and finger, and can come off easier when drying. I warned her and sure enough, same thing. So do be careful. Additionally, she finds there is a (slight) risk of stuff like soap building up in the little grooves. No worries, what little she thinks she saw (it's tiny) washed out easily. And so far, after two weeks, it continues to look like new.

In the end she really likes this Enso Rings Disney Lilo and Stitch Silicone Ring Collection and is so happy to have this Stitch ring. I've seen a few others on their pages I'd consider, so yes, we'd get another Enso ring. Always fun to wear an ode to something that makes you smile.
text_fidelity_b: Enso Rings Disney Lilo & Stitch Silicone Ring Collection - Comfortable and Flexible Design - Ohana and Experiment 626

text_fidelity_a:
Step2 Cascading Cove Sand & Water Table with Umbrella | Kids Sand & Water Play Table with Umbrella | 6-pc Accessory Set Included, Blue I looked at different types water tables and sand tables and combos and finally decided on this one. Price was unbeatable (purchased during prime day and got a great deal). I based my finally decision on the following factors:

1) Feedback: based on the feedback this seemed to be the best product out there regarding hour long entertainment, durability, quality, and price
2) Quality: It comes with a cover lid that is fastened via cords on each side allowing it to stay put during storms and it is such a tight fit that it may not let any critters in to access the water or sand
3) It is a combo: meaning it allows for versatility. You can either fill both sides with sand or water, sand and water, or rice (as per feedback when moving it indoors to keep the mess at bay and allow indoor fun during the winter months)
4) It has two drain plugs (one each side) to allow the water and/or sand to drain easily
5) Easy clean up
6) Light enough to move
7) It came with the umbrella for the times the deck has no shade. This is great to allow a little protection from the sun
8) Value and price. If you would get a water table and sandbox separate from each other you would ultimately pay more unless you are lucky and get it used or hand me down or have time to build your own sand box.

Only down side I found so far: My 17 months old son has discovered how fun it is to transfer the sand from his sand side to the water side to make mud (Thank you hubby lol). Either way it can get messy and a bit more cumbersome to clean the water side after his fun. Suggestion: drain the water and let the sun dry out the side and grab the vacuum. Simple and quickest method.

Recommendation I like to pass one from a feedback I read on another sand table product: Add a bit of cinnamon to your play sand to deter critters (in case they find a way in with the cover). It works.
text_fidelity_b: Step2 Cascading Cove Sand & Water Table with Umbrella | Kids Sand & Water Play Table with Umbrella | 6-pc Accessory Set Included, Blue

Fisher-Price 3-in-1 Bounce, Stride and Ride Elephant You do have to assemble this thing, but it’s pretty simple.

As with most toys like this, it’s a little on the loud side, but it’s not too bad. There’s been much worse noise traveling through our house with other toys.

This toy can be used 3 main ways. Your little one can sit on the seat and bounce. The seat is “bouncy”. Your little one can also push themselves along with their feet while straddling the seat. And, they can stand behind it and push it along. The handle used for pushing the car is hid underneath the elephant. To pull it out, simply push the red levers in toward each other, and it comes loose. Just snap it in place behind the elephant and it’s ready to go.

A few other features:

There are buttons to mash and light up.
It plays music and sings songs.
The elephant has cloth ears.
There IS a button to turn the volume off.

My little ones love it!
